conflicts.point: Whether mandatory collective bargaining over technological workflow updates creates paralyzing administrative deadlocks that outweigh transitional protections.

positions.stance: Mandatory impact-bargaining periods and procedural notice requirements impose a structural friction tax that halts agile software iteration.
Adapting existing labor mechanisms through the National Labor Relations Act achieves enforceable worker protection with minimal administrative overhead.

conflicts.point: Whether narrow speed-and-volume productivity metrics systematically mask the long-term collapse of institutional trust and worker agency during enterprise restructuring.

positions.stance: Rapid capability scaling and high economic dynamism generate net compensation and societal benefits that dwarf localized transitional costs.
Preserving internal diagnostic expertise and institutional guardrails is essential to prevent catastrophic operational collapse during system failures.

verdicts.conflict: Whether mandatory collective bargaining over technological workflow updates creates paralyzing administrative deadlocks that outweigh transitional protections.
verdicts.rationale: The skeptic position relies on established statutory mechanisms under the National Labor Relations Act rather than building a novel regulatory agency. This approach avoids the three-to-seven-year implementation delays historically associated with new environmental review bureaucracies.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Evidence that existing labor boards lack the technical capacity to arbitrate software deployment disputes without causing systemic commercial gridlock would flip this verdict.

verdicts.conflict: Whether narrow speed-and-volume productivity metrics systematically mask the long-term collapse of institutional trust and worker agency during enterprise restructuring.
verdicts.rationale: Historical data from aviation and rail automation demonstrates that routine cognitive offloading leads directly to operator skill atrophy. The safetyist position accounts for systemic operational failure modes that speed-and-volume metrics fail to capture.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical proof that modern foundation models maintain human situational awareness and diagnostic capability indefinitely without active cognitive engagement would overturn this conclusion.
